A cosmological observable measured in a range of redshifts can be used as a probe of a set of
cosmological parameters. Given the cosmological observable and the cosmological parameter, there
is an optimum range of redshifts where the observable can constrain the parameter in the most
eﬀective manner. For other redshift ranges the observable values may be degenerate with respect to
the cosmological parameter values and thus ineﬃcient in constraining the given parameter. These are
blind redshift ranges. We determine the optimum and the blind redshift ranges of basic cosmological
observables with respect to three cosmological parameters: the matter density parameter Ω m, the
equation of state parameter w (assumed constant), and a modiﬁed gravity parameter ga which
parametrizes a possible evolution of the eﬀective Newton’s constant asGeff (z) =GN(1+ga(1−a)2−
